_note: Advanced V2 concept questions for bit-manipulation.

questions.title: Odd bit
questions.code:
n = 13
binary n = 1101
mask = 0001

n & mask = 0001
questions.prompt: What does n & 1 tell you about an integer n?
questions.explanation: The lowest bit shows whether the number includes the 1s place. Odd numbers have that bit set to 1, and even numbers have it set to 0.

questions.title: Mask meaning
questions.code:
n    = 1010
mask = 0010

selected bit:
n & mask = 0010
questions.prompt: What does a bit mask usually do?
choices: Select or change specific bit positions
questions.explanation: A mask is a number chosen for its bit pattern. Code uses it to keep, test, turn on, or turn off specific bit positions.

questions.title: Left shift
questions.prompt: What does 1 << 3 represent in binary position terms?
questions.explanation: Left shift moves the single 1 three positions, creating the mask for bit 3.

questions.title: XOR property
questions.prompt: Why can XOR find a value that appears once when others appear twice?
choices: x ^ x cancels to 0, and 0 ^ y leaves y
questions.explanation: XOR cancels equal pairs because a value xor itself becomes 0. When every other value appears twice, the unpaired value is the one left over.

questions.title: Set bit
questions.prompt: Which operation turns on a bit without changing other bits?
questions.explanation: OR with a mask sets the selected 1 bits while leaving other positions unchanged.

questions.title: Clear bit
choices: AND with a mask that has 0 at the bit to clear
OR with the same bit mask
Convert the number to a list
questions.explanation: AND keeps positions where the mask has 1 and clears positions where the mask has 0.

questions.title: Count bits
questions.prompt: What does repeatedly using n & (n - 1) do?
choices: Removes one set bit each time
questions.explanation: The expression clears the lowest set bit, so each loop can count one 1 bit.

questions.title: Bit mistake
questions.prompt: What is a common bit manipulation mistake?
choices: Confusing bit positions with decimal digits
questions.explanation: Bits are binary positions. Decimal digits like 10 or 25 are not the same thing as bit indexes.
